Problem and behavior

Read-only Git status and diff could ask a configured promisor remote for missing objects. The corrected baseline reproduced a local upload-pack helper invocation in all three missing-object cases, with configuration writes in two disposable repositories.

This change sets `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` for every Git read-adapter invocation and extends the existing bounded, keys-only admission check to reject `extensions.partialClone`, `remote.*.promisor` and `remote.*.partialCloneFilter`. Refusals use the fixed, sanitized `GIT_UNSAFE_CONFIG` response. Ordinary remote configuration and distinct staged/unstaged diffs remain usable.

Partial-clone declarations are intentionally unsupported even when repositories are complete or declarations are false, empty, duplicated or unused. Discovery still precedes admission; no Git minimum, universal older-Git protection, alternate-object-store isolation or concurrent-writer containment is claimed.

## Validation and evidence

- The initial mixed observation and its four fixture setup failures are retained. The reviewed fixture-only repair preserves all assertions, and the corrected unchanged-production run establishes the bounded regression.
- Worker source38, independent source12 and root integration44 passed separately. The new12 cases establish 27 sanitized refusals and three ordinary successes, unchanged covered SDK manifests, absent helper markers and natural child closure.
- All seven normal root gates passed: explicit roadmap review/render/check, reviewed build/parity, typecheck, formatting and whitespace. All 121 execution bindings and 54 compiled files remain unchanged after the normal build.
- The installed Git verifier now requires exactly36 cases: preserved18 + worktree6 + new12, with all fixture and installed-module bindings. Local installed36 remains NOT_RUN; the hosted installed lanes must provide actual acceptance.
- Complete original receipts, input maps, reviews and lossless raw TAP archives are committed. Prior PR236 delivery and its corrected tracker chronology are preserved separately.

Independent integration review is CLEAR for this exact tree, with no blocking or unresolved findings. Its 53 checks cover the source, preserved catalog fields and complete evidence history. Review SHA256: `b2e7aef7101be2ba7d2aa3c6911dde8ab30ab1534d49d59217a3d7ac4b88cff5`. Candidate qualification requires all six actual jobs, including five normal installed36 lanes, security/license checks and isolated Codex configuration/MCP checks with zero model requests. After normal expected-head merge, actual main requires six separate fresh jobs.

## Scope and authorization

Refs #237 and parent #66. CLI-266, CLI-283 and CLI-284 receive evidence only; all 300 protected requirement fields, stages, seed, DCP and WEB ledgers remain unchanged.

Standing owner authorization in `docs/OWNER_AUTHORIZATION.md` covers the normal delivery workflow. Final acceptance is recorded separately after actual-main qualification. Provider lifecycle work remains held; this change performs no live provider, connected Windows, deployment or paid model operation.

Reviewed local source: `702aa061e2f95d27e7ffd3545a6fa8fada953eb0`; tree: `78f28c5f4b69ec9e1b2514c3e732fb175e51bca7`; qualified base: `c351b6146ba1d3de4a1712a886dc7300ccdc3d70`.

Published candidate: `6a6f20c2ffb350790da3d75182c33965fe9f44f7`; its tree exactly equals the reviewed local tree.

Problem and behavior

Read-only Git status and diff could ask a configured promisor remote for missing objects. The corrected baseline reproduced a local upload-pack helper invocation in all three missing-object cases, with configuration writes in two disposable repositories.

This change sets `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` for every Git read-adapter invocation and extends the existing bounded, keys-only admission check to reject `extensions.partialClone`, `remote.*.promisor` and `remote.*.partialCloneFilter`. Refusals use the fixed, sanitized `GIT_UNSAFE_CONFIG` response. Ordinary remote configuration and distinct staged/unstaged diffs remain usable.

Partial-clone declarations are intentionally unsupported even when repositories are complete or declarations are false, empty, duplicated or unused. Discovery still precedes admission; no Git minimum, universal older-Git protection, alternate-object-store isolation or concurrent-writer containment is claimed.

## Validation and evidence

- The initial mixed observation and its four fixture setup failures are retained. The reviewed fixture-only repair preserves all assertions, and the corrected unchanged-production run establishes the bounded regression.
- Worker source38, independent source12 and root integration44 passed separately. The new12 cases establish 27 sanitized refusals and three ordinary successes, unchanged covered SDK manifests, absent helper markers and natural child closure.
- All seven normal root gates passed: explicit roadmap review/render/check, reviewed build/parity, typecheck, formatting and whitespace. All 121 execution bindings and 54 compiled files remain unchanged after the normal build.
- The installed Git verifier now requires exactly36 cases: preserved18 + worktree6 + new12, with all fixture and installed-module bindings. Local installed36 remains NOT_RUN; the hosted installed lanes must provide actual acceptance.
- Complete original receipts, input maps, reviews and lossless raw TAP archives are committed. Prior PR236 delivery and its corrected tracker chronology are preserved separately.

Independent integration review is CLEAR for this exact tree, with no blocking or unresolved findings. Its 53 checks cover the source, preserved catalog fields and complete evidence history. Review SHA256: `b2e7aef7101be2ba7d2aa3c6911dde8ab30ab1534d49d59217a3d7ac4b88cff5`. Candidate qualification requires all six actual jobs, including five normal installed36 lanes, security/license checks and isolated Codex configuration/MCP checks with zero model requests. After normal expected-head merge, actual main requires six separate fresh jobs.

## Scope and authorization

Refs #237 and parent #66. CLI-266, CLI-283 and CLI-284 receive evidence only; all 300 protected requirement fields, stages, seed, DCP and WEB ledgers remain unchanged.

Standing owner authorization in `docs/OWNER_AUTHORIZATION.md` covers the normal delivery workflow. Final acceptance is recorded separately after actual-main qualification. Provider lifecycle work remains held; this change performs no live provider, connected Windows, deployment or paid model operation.

Reviewed local source: `702aa061e2f95d27e7ffd3545a6fa8fada953eb0`; tree: `78f28c5f4b69ec9e1b2514c3e732fb175e51bca7`; qualified base: `c351b6146ba1d3de4a1712a886dc7300ccdc3d70`.

Published candidate: `6a6f20c2ffb350790da3d75182c33965fe9f44f7`; its tree exactly equals the reviewed local tree.

Bounded diagnostic and correction scope

Parent #66 (AUTO-001); related immutable coverage PR #236. Qualified production base: `3077a7fe1927d1ae17aab99570832d6f9e1e3819`.

Current readonly Git admission rejects command filters and configuration includes, but does not examine the three documented promisor selector families. Git documents that missing-object lookup can start a fetch subprocess. This is a plausible mechanism to investigate, **not yet a reproduced MTerm defect or mitigation result**.

## Intended contract to freeze before execution

Readonly status and staged/unstaged diff will refuse repository declarations of `extensions.partialclone`, `remote.*.promisor`, or `remote.*.partialclonefilter` with the existing sanitized `GIT_UNSAFE_CONFIG` boundary. The key-only policy intentionally includes false or unused declarations and complete promisor repositories. Ordinary complete clone/worktree reads remain supported. Applying `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` consistently is additional protection on Git implementations that support it; this scope does not invent an enforced minimum Git version or universal older-Git support.

The current metadata-discovery-before-configuration-admission limitation must remain explicit. No general hostile-repository sandbox, universal network denial, alternates protection or concurrent-writer containment is claimed.

## Acceptance and evidence

1. Independently review and freeze a genuine promisor-pack fixture before its first product execution on unchanged production. Retain exact inputs, raw results and any invalid calibration; never manufacture a RED.
2. Use independent actual SDK/stdio status, unstaged-diff and staged-diff observations, selecting the three promisor families separately. Verify a genuinely missing HEAD tree or blob, as appropriate.
3. Calibrate native Git's local marker-only upload-pack route separately, with a real owned donor and paths containing spaces. The helper writes one small marker and exits; no credentials, external URL, listener, pack serving or helper-spawned child.
4. An error returned after marker invocation is still a failed no-fetch observation. Capture marker/object/repository state after actual natural child closure; use bounded commands and complete owned before/after manifests.
5. Add explicit complete-promisor, false/unused-declaration and ordinary-repository controls. Preserve the existing18 boundary cases and issue235's six native clone/worktree cases without weakening assertions.
6. If baseline evidence justifies correction, change only the bounded Git policy and consistently set the suppression environment. Independently review source and repeat the frozen regression.
7. Root serializes the existing installed Git verifier after PR236's separate actual-main qualification, preserving its24-case baseline and all binding/bound requirements. Require actual new installed cases across all five package lanes, six exact candidate jobs and six separate actual-main jobs.
8. Append CLI-266/283/284 evidence only; preserve all protected300-row fields, seed and DCP/WEB acceptance. Keep broader #66 open.

## Ownership and exclusions

A separate atomic claim is required before implementation. Planned worker ownership: `src/git.ts`, one new `tests/git-no-lazy-fetch.test.mjs`, and unique dated validation/AI files. Root owns the serialized verifier change, shared security/handoff/catalog records, publication and normal expected-head merge.

PR236 is frozen under read-only hosted audit. A failure there takes priority. The new worker starts from qualified3077 and cannot absorb or rewrite the unqualified candidate; final integration waits for separately qualified current main.

Bounded diagnostic and correction scope

Parent #66 (AUTO-001); related immutable coverage PR #236. Qualified production base: `3077a7fe1927d1ae17aab99570832d6f9e1e3819`.

Current readonly Git admission rejects command filters and configuration includes, but does not examine the three documented promisor selector families. Git documents that missing-object lookup can start a fetch subprocess. This is a plausible mechanism to investigate, **not yet a reproduced MTerm defect or mitigation result**.

## Intended contract to freeze before execution

Readonly status and staged/unstaged diff will refuse repository declarations of `extensions.partialclone`, `remote.*.promisor`, or `remote.*.partialclonefilter` with the existing sanitized `GIT_UNSAFE_CONFIG` boundary. The key-only policy intentionally includes false or unused declarations and complete promisor repositories. Ordinary complete clone/worktree reads remain supported. Applying `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` consistently is additional protection on Git implementations that support it; this scope does not invent an enforced minimum Git version or universal older-Git support.

The current metadata-discovery-before-configuration-admission limitation must remain explicit. No general hostile-repository sandbox, universal network denial, alternates protection or concurrent-writer containment is claimed.

## Acceptance and evidence

1. Independently review and freeze a genuine promisor-pack fixture before its first product execution on unchanged production. Retain exact inputs, raw results and any invalid calibration; never manufacture a RED.
2. Use independent actual SDK/stdio status, unstaged-diff and staged-diff observations, selecting the three promisor families separately. Verify a genuinely missing HEAD tree or blob, as appropriate.
3. Calibrate native Git's local marker-only upload-pack route separately, with a real owned donor and paths containing spaces. The helper writes one small marker and exits; no credentials, external URL, listener, pack serving or helper-spawned child.
4. An error returned after marker invocation is still a failed no-fetch observation. Capture marker/object/repository state after actual natural child closure; use bounded commands and complete owned before/after manifests.
5. Add explicit complete-promisor, false/unused-declaration and ordinary-repository controls. Preserve the existing18 boundary cases and issue235's six native clone/worktree cases without weakening assertions.
6. If baseline evidence justifies correction, change only the bounded Git policy and consistently set the suppression environment. Independently review source and repeat the frozen regression.
7. Root serializes the existing installed Git verifier after PR236's separate actual-main qualification, preserving its24-case baseline and all binding/bound requirements. Require actual new installed cases across all five package lanes, six exact candidate jobs and six separate actual-main jobs.
8. Append CLI-266/283/284 evidence only; preserve all protected300-row fields, seed and DCP/WEB acceptance. Keep broader #66 open.

## Ownership and exclusions

A separate atomic claim is required before implementation. Planned worker ownership: `src/git.ts`, one new `tests/git-no-lazy-fetch.test.mjs`, and unique dated validation/AI files. Root owns the serialized verifier change, shared security/handoff/catalog records, publication and normal expected-head merge.

PR236 is frozen under read-only hosted audit. A failure there takes priority. The new worker starts from qualified3077 and cannot absorb or rewrite the unqualified candidate; final integration waits for separately qualified current main.

No dependencies, workflows, product roots, CLI permissions, provider writes, Windows workstation actions, production bridge, global toolchain, paid/model lane or unrelated-project operation is included. Standing owner authorization applies.

Bounded diagnostic and correction scope

Parent #66 (AUTO-001); related immutable coverage PR #236. Qualified production base: `3077a7fe1927d1ae17aab99570832d6f9e1e3819`.

Current readonly Git admission rejects command filters and configuration includes, but does not examine the three documented promisor selector families. Git documents that missing-object lookup can start a fetch subprocess. This is a plausible mechanism to investigate, **not yet a reproduced MTerm defect or mitigation result**.

## Intended contract to freeze before execution

Readonly status and staged/unstaged diff will refuse repository declarations of `extensions.partialclone`, `remote.*.promisor`, or `remote.*.partialclonefilter` with the existing sanitized `GIT_UNSAFE_CONFIG` boundary. The key-only policy intentionally includes false or unused declarations and complete promisor repositories. Ordinary complete clone/worktree reads remain supported. Applying `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` consistently is additional protection on Git implementations that support it; this scope does not invent an enforced minimum Git version or universal older-Git support.

The current metadata-discovery-before-configuration-admission limitation must remain explicit. No general hostile-repository sandbox, universal network denial, alternates protection or concurrent-writer containment is claimed.

## Acceptance and evidence

1. Independently review and freeze a genuine promisor-pack fixture before its first product execution on unchanged production. Retain exact inputs, raw results and any invalid calibration; never manufacture a RED.
2. Use independent actual SDK/stdio status, unstaged-diff and staged-diff observations, selecting the three promisor families separately. Verify a genuinely missing HEAD tree or blob, as appropriate.
3. Calibrate native Git's local marker-only upload-pack route separately, with a real owned donor and paths containing spaces. The helper writes one small marker and exits; no credentials, external URL, listener, pack serving or helper-spawned child.
4. An error returned after marker invocation is still a failed no-fetch observation. Capture marker/object/repository state after actual natural child closure; use bounded commands and complete owned before/after manifests.
5. Add explicit complete-promisor, false/unused-declaration and ordinary-repository controls. Preserve the existing18 boundary cases and issue235's six native clone/worktree cases without weakening assertions.
6. If baseline evidence justifies correction, change only the bounded Git policy and consistently set the suppression environment. Independently review source and repeat the frozen regression.
7. Root serializes the existing installed Git verifier after PR236's separate actual-main qualification, preserving its24-case baseline and all binding/bound requirements. Require actual new installed cases across all five package lanes, six exact candidate jobs and six separate actual-main jobs.
8. Append CLI-266/283/284 evidence only; preserve all protected300-row fields, seed and DCP/WEB acceptance. Keep broader #66 open.

## Ownership and exclusions

A separate atomic claim is required before implementation. Planned worker ownership: `src/git.ts`, one new `tests/git-no-lazy-fetch.test.mjs`, and unique dated validation/AI files. Root owns the serialized verifier change, shared security/handoff/catalog records, publication and normal expected-head merge.

PR236 is frozen under read-only hosted audit. A failure there takes priority. The new worker starts from qualified3077 and cannot absorb or rewrite the unqualified candidate; final integration waits for separately qualified current main.

No dependencies, workflows, product roots, CLI permissions, provider writes, Windows workstation actions, production bridge, global toolchain, paid/model lane or unrelated-project operation is included. Standing owner authorization applies.

Problem and behavior

Read-only Git status and diff could ask a configured promisor remote for missing objects. The corrected baseline reproduced a local upload-pack helper invocation in all three missing-object cases, with configuration writes in two disposable repositories.

This change sets `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` for every Git read-adapter invocation and extends the existing bounded, keys-only admission check to reject `extensions.partialClone`, `remote.*.promisor` and `remote.*.partialCloneFilter`. Refusals use the fixed, sanitized `GIT_UNSAFE_CONFIG` response. Ordinary remote configuration and distinct staged/unstaged diffs remain usable.

Partial-clone declarations are intentionally unsupported even when repositories are complete or declarations are false, empty, duplicated or unused. Discovery still precedes admission; no Git minimum, universal older-Git protection, alternate-object-store isolation or concurrent-writer containment is claimed.

## Validation and evidence

- The initial mixed observation and its four fixture setup failures are retained. The reviewed fixture-only repair preserves all assertions, and the corrected unchanged-production run establishes the bounded regression.
- Worker source38, independent source12 and root integration44 passed separately. The new12 cases establish 27 sanitized refusals and three ordinary successes, unchanged covered SDK manifests, absent helper markers and natural child closure.
- All seven normal root gates passed: explicit roadmap review/render/check, reviewed build/parity, typecheck, formatting and whitespace. All 121 execution bindings and 54 compiled files remain unchanged after the normal build.
- The installed Git verifier now requires exactly36 cases: preserved18 + worktree6 + new12, with all fixture and installed-module bindings. Local installed36 remains NOT_RUN; the hosted installed lanes must provide actual acceptance.
- Complete original receipts, input maps, reviews and lossless raw TAP archives are committed. Prior PR236 delivery and its corrected tracker chronology are preserved separately.

Independent integration review is CLEAR for this exact tree, with no blocking or unresolved findings. Its 53 checks cover the source, preserved catalog fields and complete evidence history. Review SHA256: `b2e7aef7101be2ba7d2aa3c6911dde8ab30ab1534d49d59217a3d7ac4b88cff5`. Candidate qualification requires all six actual jobs, including five normal installed36 lanes, security/license checks and isolated Codex configuration/MCP checks with zero model requests. After normal expected-head merge, actual main requires six separate fresh jobs.

## Scope and authorization

Refs #237 and parent #66. CLI-266, CLI-283 and CLI-284 receive evidence only; all 300 protected requirement fields, stages, seed, DCP and WEB ledgers remain unchanged.

Standing owner authorization in `docs/OWNER_AUTHORIZATION.md` covers the normal delivery workflow. Final acceptance is recorded separately after actual-main qualification. Provider lifecycle work remains held; this change performs no live provider, connected Windows, deployment or paid model operation.

Problem and behavior

Read-only Git status and diff could ask a configured promisor remote for missing objects. The corrected baseline reproduced a local upload-pack helper invocation in all three missing-object cases, with configuration writes in two disposable repositories.

This change sets `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` for every Git read-adapter invocation and extends the existing bounded, keys-only admission check to reject `extensions.partialClone`, `remote.*.promisor` and `remote.*.partialCloneFilter`. Refusals use the fixed, sanitized `GIT_UNSAFE_CONFIG` response. Ordinary remote configuration and distinct staged/unstaged diffs remain usable.

Partial-clone declarations are intentionally unsupported even when repositories are complete or declarations are false, empty, duplicated or unused. Discovery still precedes admission; no Git minimum, universal older-Git protection, alternate-object-store isolation or concurrent-writer containment is claimed.

## Validation and evidence

- The initial mixed observation and its four fixture setup failures are retained. The reviewed fixture-only repair preserves all assertions, and the corrected unchanged-production run establishes the bounded regression.
- Worker source38, independent source12 and root integration44 passed separately. The new12 cases establish 27 sanitized refusals and three ordinary successes, unchanged covered SDK manifests, absent helper markers and natural child closure.
- All seven normal root gates passed: explicit roadmap review/render/check, reviewed build/parity, typecheck, formatting and whitespace. All 121 execution bindings and 54 compiled files remain unchanged after the normal build.
- The installed Git verifier now requires exactly36 cases: preserved18 + worktree6 + new12, with all fixture and installed-module bindings. Local installed36 remains NOT_RUN; the hosted installed lanes must provide actual acceptance.
- Complete original receipts, input maps, reviews and lossless raw TAP archives are committed. Prior PR236 delivery and its corrected tracker chronology are preserved separately.

Independent integration review is CLEAR for this exact tree, with no blocking or unresolved findings. Its 53 checks cover the source, preserved catalog fields and complete evidence history. Review SHA256: `b2e7aef7101be2ba7d2aa3c6911dde8ab30ab1534d49d59217a3d7ac4b88cff5`. Candidate qualification requires all six actual jobs, including five normal installed36 lanes, security/license checks and isolated Codex configuration/MCP checks with zero model requests. After normal expected-head merge, actual main requires six separate fresh jobs.

## Scope and authorization

Refs #237 and parent #66. CLI-266, CLI-283 and CLI-284 receive evidence only; all 300 protected requirement fields, stages, seed, DCP and WEB ledgers remain unchanged.

Standing owner authorization in `docs/OWNER_AUTHORIZATION.md` covers the normal delivery workflow. Final acceptance is recorded separately after actual-main qualification. Provider lifecycle work remains held; this change performs no live provider, connected Windows, deployment or paid model operation.

## Final acceptance — bounded issue 237 slice

Session `MTERM-WEB-20261109T131339Z-resume-a9287b3c`; OpenAI / GPT-6 Astra Pro, ChatGPT Web (self-reported).

PR #238 was normally merged at expected candidate `6a6f20c2ffb350790da3d75182c33965fe9f44f7`. Actual main `9c05ed3fd92ee87dcc789a81a8c605e62fe7f141` has the same reviewed tree `78f28c5f4b69ec9e1b2514c3e732fb175e51bca7`, with separately qualified base `c351b6146ba1d3de4a1712a886dc7300ccdc3d70` and the published candidate as its parents.

The candidate and actual main each passed six separate hosted jobs. Main push attempt 1 ran [fast CI](https://github.com/MulattoTech/MTerm-CLI/actions/runs/42713279271) and [compatibility/native CI](https://github.com/MulattoTech/MTerm-CLI/actions/runs/42713279138); all six jobs and every step succeeded. All logs checked out actual main directly. The five full source suites each contained 1,275 cases: Windows passed all 1,275; the other four passed 1,263 with the same 12 existing Windows-only skips. All 537 required titles occurred exactly once per suite. Five actual installed-package lanes passed the 36-case Git contract; four actual pinned Codex 0.160.1 registration/MCP lanes made zero model calls. The fresh native archive separately established 12 source cases, 12 installed cases and 31 protocol cases, with owned scenario and OOM cleanup evidence.

Independent actual-main review: 105 checks, no findings (`588736afd335e073287138ca5c89ce10e6ffb2cafa87d9be05b69401b26b4972`). Independent native component: 66 checks, no findings (`e9bd807691de1e90abe53b17833c2b9d29d733593dded3aec65cb6c643573d7e`). Root rehashed 91 bound evidence files, all 858 source blobs and Git identities, and all 54 qualified compiled files; clean actual main matches the reviewed tree. Root final check: `7dfb48517438b6efe115ef3dda1192603c4c3f988e29b07cca1bbf4050fd72e3`. A fresh authenticated read immediately before this acceptance still showed issue 237 open, its original claim active, actual main unchanged and all six main checks successful.

Acceptance is limited to setting the child Git no-lazy-fetch environment guard and rejecting the bounded partial-clone/promisor declaration keys for supported read-only operations, with the preserved baseline/fixture evidence and ordinary repository compatibility. It does not establish a universal guarantee for older Git, pre-admission discovery, alternates, concurrent repository changes or arbitrary network activity; parent #66 remains open. Protected requirement/stage credit is unchanged. No provider or connected Windows operation, deployment or model-consuming worker was used for this slice.

Evidence limits remain explicit: raw installed Git 36-case TAP and native runtime/DEB bytes were not in the retrieved hosted artifacts; no independent raw TAP rehash or fresh offline DEB signature verification is claimed. Local installed/full/quick suites were not rerun. The originally mixed fixture and the corrected valid RED are retained separately. The source evidence is already in the merged tree; the immutable final delivery appendix will accompany the next serialized integration.

This comment records acceptance after the complete actual-main review. Root will next mark the preserved claim inactive and explicitly complete this narrow issue.

issue.title: [P1][AUTO-001] Bound implicit fetching during read-only Git inspection
issue.body:
## Bounded diagnostic and correction scope

Parent #66 (AUTO-001); related immutable coverage PR #236. Qualified production base: `3077a7fe1927d1ae17aab99570832d6f9e1e3819`.

Current readonly Git admission rejects command filters and configuration includes, but does not examine the three documented promisor selector families. Git documents that missing-object lookup can start a fetch subprocess. This is a plausible mechanism to investigate, **not yet a reproduced MTerm defect or mitigation result**.

## Intended contract to freeze before execution

Readonly status and staged/unstaged diff will refuse repository declarations of `extensions.partialclone`, `remote.*.promisor`, or `remote.*.partialclonefilter` with the existing sanitized `GIT_UNSAFE_CONFIG` boundary. The key-only policy intentionally includes false or unused declarations and complete promisor repositories. Ordinary complete clone/worktree reads remain supported. Applying `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` consistently is additional protection on Git implementations that support it; this scope does not invent an enforced minimum Git version or universal older-Git support.

The current metadata-discovery-before-configuration-admission limitation must remain explicit. No general hostile-repository sandbox, universal network denial, alternates protection or concurrent-writer containment is claimed.

## Acceptance and evidence

1. Independently review and freeze a genuine promisor-pack fixture before its first product execution on unchanged production. Retain exact inputs, raw results and any invalid calibration; never manufacture a RED.
2. Use independent actual SDK/stdio status, unstaged-diff and staged-diff observations, selecting the three promisor families separately. Verify a genuinely missing HEAD tree or blob, as appropriate.
3. Calibrate native Git's local marker-only upload-pack route separately, with a real owned donor and paths containing spaces. The helper writes one small marker and exits; no credentials, external URL, listener, pack serving or helper-spawned child.
4. An error returned after marker invocation is still a failed no-fetch observation. Capture marker/object/repository state after actual natural child closure; use bounded commands and complete owned before/after manifests.
5. Add explicit complete-promisor, false/unused-declaration and ordinary-repository controls. Preserve the existing18 boundary cases and issue235's six native clone/worktree cases without weakening assertions.
6. If baseline evidence justifies correction, change only the bounded Git policy and consistently set the suppression environment. Independently review source and repeat the frozen regression.
7. Root serializes the existing installed Git verifier after PR236's separate actual-main qualification, preserving its24-case baseline and all binding/bound requirements. Require actual new installed cases across all five package lanes, six exact candidate jobs and six separate actual-main jobs.
8. Append CLI-266/283/284 evidence only; preserve all protected300-row fields, seed and DCP/WEB acceptance. Keep broader #66 open.

## Ownership and exclusions

4. An error returned after marker invocation is still a failed no-fetch observation. Capture marker/object/repository state after actual natural child closure; use bounded commands and complete owned before/after manifests.
5. Add explicit complete-promisor, false/unused-declaration and ordinary-repository controls. Preserve the existing18 boundary cases and issue235's six native clone/worktree cases without weakening assertions.
6. If baseline evidence justifies correction, change only the bounded Git policy and consistently set the suppression environment. Independently review source and repeat the frozen regression.

8. Append CLI-266/283/284 evidence only; preserve all protected300-row fields, seed and DCP/WEB acceptance. Keep broader #66 open.

A separate atomic claim is required before implementation. Planned worker ownership: `src/git.ts`, one new `tests/git-no-lazy-fetch.test.mjs`, and unique dated validation/AI files. Root owns the serialized verifier change, shared security/handoff/catalog records, publication and normal expected-head merge.

Problem

The MJobs/DevFleet-style automation creates isolated Git worktrees. In a linked worktree, `.git` is a pointer file and Git metadata lives in the parent repository's common directory. MTerm's current Git inspection rejects the external metadata with `GIT_OUTSIDE_ROOT`. During the 2026-10-16 HAR/automation validation, normal build/tests/package/Codex registration passed but `verify-self-host.mjs` failed when run from an intentionally linked worktree.

## Required acceptance

- Preserve the default trusted-root and link/reparse protections; do not permit arbitrary Git metadata escapes.
- Explicitly recognize valid linked worktrees only when the worktree and its canonical common Git directory are independently authorized or are owned by a verified setup.
- Test malformed .git pointer files, adversarial symlinks, unrelated repository Git directory redirection, unsafe config/hooks and cross-workspace abuse.
- Read-only `git status`/`git diff` through installed MCP work safely in both a normal clone and an authorized linked worktree; denied cases remain denied.
- Separate credentials, prompts, OS permissions and Codex execution policy from Git metadata authorization.
- Update DCP/CLI metrics only after full acceptance and platform tests.

**Current state:** open/NOT PASS; a temporary normal-clone verification workaround is acceptable but not parity completion. Problem and behavior

Read-only Git status and diff could ask a configured promisor remote for missing objects. The corrected baseline reproduced a local upload-pack helper invocation in all three missing-object cases, with configuration writes in two disposable repositories.

This change sets `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` for every Git read-adapter invocation and extends the existing bounded, keys-only admission check to reject `extensions.partialClone`, `remote.*.promisor` and `remote.*.partialCloneFilter`. Refusals use the fixed, sanitized `GIT_UNSAFE_CONFIG` response. Ordinary remote configuration and distinct staged/unstaged diffs remain usable.

Partial-clone declarations are intentionally unsupported even when repositories are complete or declarations are false, empty, duplicated or unused. Discovery still precedes admission; no Git minimum, universal older-Git protection, alternate-object-store isolation or concurrent-writer containment is claimed.

## Validation and evidence

- The initial mixed observation and its four fixture setup failures are retained. The reviewed fixture-only repair preserves all assertions, and the corrected unchanged-production run establishes the bounded regression.
- Worker source38, independent source12 and root integration44 passed separately. The new12 cases establish 27 sanitized refusals and three ordinary successes, unchanged covered SDK manifests, absent helper markers and natural child closure.
- All seven normal root gates passed: explicit roadmap review/render/check, reviewed build/parity, typecheck, formatting and whitespace. All 121 execution bindings and 54 compiled files remain unchanged after the normal build.
- The installed Git verifier now requires exactly36 cases: preserved18 + worktree6 + new12, with all fixture and installed-module bindings. Local installed36 remains NOT_RUN; the hosted installed lanes must provide actual acceptance.
- Complete original receipts, input maps, reviews and lossless raw TAP archives are committed. Prior PR236 delivery and its corrected tracker chronology are preserved separately.

Independent integration review is CLEAR for this exact tree, with no blocking or unresolved findings. Its 53 checks cover the source, preserved catalog fields and complete evidence history. Review SHA256: `b2e7aef7101be2ba7d2aa3c6911dde8ab30ab1534d49d59217a3d7ac4b88cff5`. Candidate qualification requires all six actual jobs, including five normal installed36 lanes, security/license checks and isolated Codex configuration/MCP checks with zero model requests. After normal expected-head merge, actual main requires six separate fresh jobs.

## Scope and authorization

The MJobs/DevFleet-style automation creates isolated Git worktrees. In a linked worktree, `.git` is a pointer file and Git metadata lives in the parent repository's common directory. - Test malformed .git pointer files, adversarial symlinks, unrelated repository Git directory redirection, unsafe config/hooks and cross-workspace abuse.
- Read-only `git status`/`git diff` through installed MCP work safely in both a normal clone and an authorized linked worktree; denied cases remain denied.
- Separate credentials, prompts, OS permissions and Codex execution policy from Git metadata authorization.
- Update DCP/CLI metrics only after full acceptance and platform tests.

Problem and relationship

Child of #66 (AUTO-001). The existing Git boundary suite demonstrates the common-metadata and filter denials delivered by PR #212, but its positive linked fixture rearranges Git's private admin layout and calls GitService directly. It does not qualify successful read-only Git inspection through an installed SDK/stdio MCP server in an untouched Git-created linked worktree.

This slice adds that missing qualification. Source inspection suggests existing behavior already supports explicitly granting the worktree and its actual parent repository; that remains an inference until the new fixture executes. Broader #66 remains open.

## Scope and ownership

Session: `MTERM-WEB-20261109T131339Z-resume-a9287b3c`.
Provider/model: OpenAI / GPT-6 Astra Pro, ChatGPT Web (self-reported).
Starting qualified main: `c69762da7d1dda54f7a74795c08c1f699367c77f`.

- `tests/git-worktree-mcp.test.mjs`
- `scripts/verify-package.mjs` (existing Git block only)
- `docs/validation/2026-11-09-installed-worktree.md`
- `docs/ai/changes/2026-11-09-installed-worktree.json`

Root owns serialized shared documentation, roadmap review, integration and publication. PR #234 is frozen for independent hosted review on disjoint source paths. This child may develop isolated tests while that review runs; no integration/merge will race #234, and its separately qualified actual main must be reconciled before publication.

## Acceptance

1. Use disposable local repositories with a normal independent clone and ordinary `git worktree add --detach`. Preserve the native .git pointer, gitdir and commondir topology; do not relocate metadata or rewrite pointers.
2. Use real SDK/stdio MCP calls and `MTERM_VERIFY_BIN` for the installed entry. Run the installed child from an external owned cwd/home with no write or general-execution grants.
3. Normal clone: status, unstaged diff and staged diff return exact expected staged/unstaged/untracked entries. Distinct sentinel files prove staged and unstaged results do not contaminate each other.
4. Ordinary linked worktree with explicit worktree plus actual parent-repository roots: the same operations succeed at top-level and nested request paths. No common-parent blanket grant or implicit root discovery.
5. Worktree-only and worktree-plus-unrelated-repository grants: all three operations return `GIT_OUTSIDE_ROOT`. Denial assertions retain safe bounded responses without exposing private diagnostics or successful file contents.
6. Even with the correct explicit pair, ordinary file-tool reads of the .git pointer and parent .git/config remain `PRIVATE_PATH`; mutating filesystem and process tools remain unavailable.
7. Exact relevant file and Git metadata manifests before/after the MCP observation interval remain equal. Own and bound every child; require observed natural close, empty/unexpected-error-free stderr as applicable, and cleanup.
8. Extend the existing installed-package Git verification block, retaining the original 18-case fixture and its hash, adding the reviewed new fixture hash and exact combined count, and reporting only observations actually asserted.
9. Preserve production source, RootPolicy, CLI options, dependency locks, workflows, original tests and self-host verifier.

## Evidence discipline and gates

Freeze and independently review the fixture before its first execution against unchanged qualified production source. If it passes immediately, retain an honest GREEN characterization of existing behavior; do not manufacture RED. If it fails, retain exact input hashes and TAP, distinguish fixture/setup defects from product failures, and stop for root to rescope before any production edit. Do not weaken roots, expected denials or native layout to obtain success.

Run focused source and actual installed-package checks, independent review, normal roadmap/build/typecheck/format/parity gates, all six exact candidate hosted jobs and all six separate actual-main jobs. Keep source/installed bytes and raw evidence bound to exact commits. No model calls or live provider/Windows operations.

Requirements: CLI-266, CLI-283 and CLI-284. Append bounded evidence only; preserve all protected catalog fields, current stages and the 300-ID seed. No DCP/WEB acceptance is earned.

## Remaining work outside this child

Malformed/adversarial pointer ownership, alternates, partial-clone implicit fetches, configuration consulted during initial native discovery, full cross-workspace relationship proof, hostile repository sandboxing and concurrent writer races are not qualified here. Existing filter/include and metadata-file protections remain in force.

## Authority and next action

Standing owner authorization in `docs/OWNER_AUTHORIZATION.md` covers this workflow; no repeat manual approval is pending. The MJobs/DevFleet-style automation creates isolated Git worktrees. In a linked worktree, `.git` is a pointer file and Git metadata lives in the parent repository's common directory. MTerm's current Git inspection rejects the external metadata with `GIT_OUTSIDE_ROOT`. During the 2026-10-16 HAR/automation validation, normal build/tests/package/Codex registration passed but `verify-self-host.mjs` failed when run from an intentionally linked worktree.

## Required acceptance

- Preserve the default trusted-root and link/reparse protections; do not permit arbitrary Git metadata escapes.
- Explicitly recognize valid linked worktrees only when the worktree and its canonical common Git directory are independently authorized or are owned by a verified setup.
- Test malformed .git pointer files, adversarial symlinks, unrelated repository Git directory redirection, unsafe config/hooks and cross-workspace abuse.
- Read-only `git status`/`git diff` through installed MCP work safely in both a normal clone and an authorized linked worktree; denied cases remain denied.
- Separate credentials, prompts, OS permissions and Codex execution policy from Git metadata authorization.
- Update DCP/CLI metrics only after full acceptance and platform tests.

**Current state:** open/NOT PASS; a temporary normal-clone verification workaround is acceptable but not parity completion.
